items.followUp: What happens to an enzyme’s active site when the enzyme is denatured?

rubric.why: Identifies a factor that can denature an enzyme.
rubric.description: Names a cause of enzyme denaturation.
rubric.how: Award for naming a valid cause, such as high temperature, extreme pH, or certain chemicals.

rubric.why: Explains how denaturation affects enzyme structure and function.
rubric.description: States that the enzyme’s shape changes and it can no longer catalyse the reaction.
rubric.how: Award for explaining that the structural change, especially at the active site, prevents the enzyme from catalysing its reaction.

modelAnswer: High temperature, an extreme pH, or certain chemicals can change an enzyme’s three-dimensional structure.
The active site changes shape, so the enzyme can no longer catalyse its reaction.

items.followUp: Name two types of stains that enzymes in biological detergents can remove.

rubric.why: Identifies a detergent enzyme that acts on protein-based stains.
rubric.description: Names proteases and their stain target.
rubric.how: Award for stating that proteases break down protein stains, such as blood stains.

rubric.why: Identifies a detergent enzyme that acts on fats or grease.
rubric.description: Names lipases and their stain target.
rubric.how: Award for stating that lipases break down fat or grease stains.

modelAnswer: Proteases in biological detergents break down protein stains such as blood.
Lipases break down fat and grease stains.

items.followUp: What is the main energy-storing product of cellular respiration?

rubric.why: Identifies the breakdown of food, especially glucose, as the process of respiration.
rubric.description: Defines cellular respiration as the breakdown of food molecules in cells.
rubric.how: Award for stating that cells break down food or glucose during cellular respiration.

rubric.why: States the outcome of respiration for the cell.
rubric.description: Explains that respiration releases energy, which is captured in ATP.
rubric.how: Award for mentioning released energy and its capture or storage in ATP.

modelAnswer: Cellular respiration is the process in which cells break down food molecules, especially glucose.
Energy is released and captured in ATP for the cell’s activities.

items.followUp: Where does glycolysis occur, and what are its main products from one glucose molecule?

rubric.why: Identifies the main products and energy yield of glycolysis.
rubric.description: States that glycolysis produces two pyruvic acid molecules and a net gain of two ATP.
rubric.how: Award for the two pyruvic acid molecules and the net gain of two ATP.

modelAnswer: Glycolysis is a series of reactions in the cytoplasm in which one glucose molecule is broken down.
It forms two molecules of pyruvic acid and gives a net gain of two ATP molecules.

items.followUp: Define enzymes and describe one use of an enzyme in the food industry and one in detergents.

rubric.why: States the defining catalytic role of enzymes.
rubric.how: Award for defining enzymes as catalysts that speed up reactions without being used up.

rubric.why: Gives a valid use of enzymes in food production.
rubric.description: Describes the use of rennin in cheese-making.
rubric.how: Award for stating that rennin coagulates milk during cheese-making.

rubric.why: Gives a specific use of enzymes in biological detergents.
rubric.description: Describes enzymes breaking down stains in detergents.
rubric.how: Award for correctly matching proteases with protein stains or lipases with fats and grease.

rubric.why: Recognizes further industrial applications of enzymes.
rubric.description: Names other industries that use enzymes.
rubric.how: Award for naming at least two of textile, leather, and paper processing.

modelAnswer: Enzymes are biological catalysts that speed up chemical reactions without being used up.
In the food industry, rennin is used to coagulate milk during cheese-making.
Proteases in detergents break down protein stains, while lipases break down fats and grease.
Enzymes are also used in textile, leather, and paper processing.
